title: Replace string-built SQL with Dapper
summary: Turn a search that concatenated values into SQL into Dapper QueryAsync<T> with an anonymous parameter object, then allow several statuses.

turns.user: the OrderRepository search glues strings into SQL and static analysis is yelling. dapper is already referenced, rewrite it with that. make it async while youre there

assistant.body: Sure thing! The values stop being concatenated into the SQL and become @customerCode and @status placeholders. Pass the values as an anonymous object and Dapper sends each property as a parameter with the same name. A value can never be read as part of the SQL, so the query is robust against injection. QueryAsync<Order> maps rows to Order by column name, so the reader loop goes away too.

turns.user: works. now they want to filter by several statuses, like paid and shipped together

assistant.body: Make the argument a collection and write IN @statuses in the SQL. When Dapper sees an IEnumerable value it expands it into @statuses1, @statuses2 and so on, and adds the parentheses itself. In other words, you do not write IN (@statuses). Note: an empty collection makes Dapper emit a condition that is always false, so you get zero rows rather than an error.
